nina: quick heads-up - docs PR #2599 (cache architecture + migration note) is blocked. We need clarification on eviction policy differences between Hosted and Dedicated before approving.

rob: what's the specific doc wording that's causing the hold?

nina: the migration guide says "cache entries are evicted by LRU when capacity is reached" but internal notes say Dedicated customers on older stacks use a time-based rolling window eviction, and Private can be configured to use either. Reviewers want exact semantics per deployment mode so they can set expectations.

steph: oof. reviewers are asking whether customers should assume LRU or time-window. Also want guidance on how TTL interacts with eviction (does eviction ignore TTL?).

docs-reviewer-amelia: yes - we need a crisp bullet list. If we leave it vague we'll get bug reports. Also request an example config showing how to opt into time-based behavior for Private.

runtime-bot: runtime note: current deployed behavior (short): Hosted uses approximate LRU with size-aware eviction (entries scored by last-access + weight). Dedicated (older fleets) use a time-window evictor (rotate segments every N minutes) which approximates TTL-driven eviction and can evict recently-used items during window rotation. Private deploys default to LRU but can be configured to use the time-window evictor via the `evictor.type` flag.

rob: can we be more concrete? e.g., how does TTL interact: if TTL is 60s but time-window rotation is 5m, will an expired item remain until rotation?

runtime-bot: yes - if TTL is set, runtime still checks TTL on read and treats items older than TTL as expired. However, time-window evictor may not immediately reclaim the disk/memory until the next rotation; reads will see the entry as expired and trigger a cache-miss. In other words: TTL is authoritative for validity; eviction affects reclaiming resources, not logical expiration.

steph: good. that means docs should say "TTL controls validity; eviction controls memory reclaiming and may lag TTL on some Dedicated configurations." Add a short example to show mismatch.

nina: drafting example text now. Also need to cover size-aware eviction: Hosted's LRU is weight-aware; can we provide an example `max_weight` config and explain weight is roughly payload bytes + metadata.

runtime-bot: hosted specifics: default `max_weight` = 10GB (tenant-wide). Weights approximate on-disk size: payload_bytes + 128B metadata. Eviction prefers dropping highest cost / least recently used entries. No strong guarantees on exact order during heavy pressure.

rob: ok. docs reviewer wants a small JSON snippet for Private config to opt into time-window evictor and a CLI example to query current evictor type for Dedicated (helpful for debugging).

steph: adding snippets: config snippet: ```yaml
cache:
  evictor:
    type: time_window # options: lru, time_window
    window_minutes: 5
    max_weight: 10737418240 # 10GB
```

cli snippet to query: ```bash
# query runtime status
redwoodctl cache status --env dedicated-fleet-1
# response will include: evictor.type: time_window, window_minutes: 5, max_weight: 10737418240
```

docs-reviewer-amelia: also add a short troubleshooting note: "If customers see cache-hit but TTL seems expired, check whether you're looking at an older Dedicated fleet with time-window evictor; read semantics still enforce TTL so treat as cache-miss."

nina: adding that. CI: pinging docs-preview after wording + snippets.

ci-bot: docs-preview: linkcheck passed. linter flagged long code fence without language on YAML snippet.

nina: fixed fence language. pushed update.

ci-bot: docs-preview: all checks passed.

docs-reviewer-amelia: re-reviewing. Looks good. Two minor asks: 1) include note that `evictor.type` change in Private requires restart and may have data-loss implications; 2) confirm runtime will not change Hosted LRU this release.

runtime-bot: confirmation: switching evictor requires node restart and caches will be reinitialized (possible cold start). Runtime will not change Hosted eviction strategy in this release. Any change needs RFC.

nina: added restart note and migration caution. Pushing final.

docs-reviewer-amelia: approved. merge on green.

ci-bot: docs-preview: all checks passed.

nina: merging now. thanks everyone! :rocket:

eng-infra-bot: FYI: we ran a quick audit on Dedicated fleets; flagged two older clusters still on time_window evictor - ops already paged owners.
